sanskrit: kṛṣṇau cāpi maheṣvāsāv abhivādya halāyudham sasvajāte pariprītau priyamāṇau yaśasvinau
english: The two Kṛṣṇas as well, those mighty archers, saluted Halāyudha; greatly delighted and full of affection, the two glorious ones embraced him.

sanskrit: mādrīputrau tathā śūrau draupadyāḥ pañca cātmajāḥ abhivādya sthitā rājan rauhiṇeyaṃ mahābalam
english: The two valiant sons of Mādrī, and the five sons of Draupadī, having saluted the mighty son of Rohiṇī, stood waiting, O king.

sanskrit: bhīmaseno 'tha balavān putras tava janādhipa tathaiva codyatagadau pūjayām āsatur balam
english: Then the powerful Bhīmasena, and your son too, O lord of men, both with maces upraised, paid honour to the strong one.

sanskrit: svāgatena ca te tatra pratipūjya punaḥ punaḥ paśya yuddhaṃ mahābāho iti te rāmam abruvan evam ūcur mahātmānaṃ rauhiṇeyaṃ narādhipāḥ
english: Honouring him there again and again with words of welcome, the kings said to Rāma, "Behold the combat, O mighty-armed one!" — thus did the rulers of men address the great-souled son of Rohiṇī.

sanskrit: pariṣvajya tadā rāmaḥ pāṇḍavān sṛñjayān api apṛcchat kuśalaṃ sarvān pāṇḍavāṃś cāmitaujasaḥ tathaiva te samāsādya papracchus tam anāmayam
english: Then Rāma, embracing the Pāṇḍavas and the Sṛñjayas as well, asked after the welfare of all those Pāṇḍavas of measureless might; and they in turn, approaching him, inquired after his good health.

sanskrit: pratyabhyarcya halī sarvān kṣatriyāṃś ca mahāmanāḥ kṛtvā kuśalasaṃyuktāṃ saṃvidaṃ ca yathāvayaḥ
english: The plough-bearer, great of mind, returned the honour to all the kṣatriyas, exchanging cordial greetings of welfare each according to his age.

sanskrit: janārdanaṃ sātyakiṃ ca premṇā sa pariṣasvaje mūrdhni caitāv upāghrāya kuśalaṃ paryapṛcchata
english: Janārdana and Sātyaki he embraced with love, and kissing the two upon the head, he inquired after their welfare.

sanskrit: tau cainaṃ vidhivad rājan pūjayām āsatur gurum brahmāṇam iva deveśam indropendrau mudā yutau
english: And those two, O king, honoured him in due form as their elder, as Indra and Upendra, filled with joy, would honour Brahmā, the lord of the gods.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīd dharmasuto rauhiṇeyam ariṃdamam idaṃ bhrātror mahāyuddhaṃ paśya rāmeti bhārata
english: Then the son of Dharma said to the son of Rohiṇī, that tamer of foes, "Behold this great combat of the two brothers, O Rāma!" — so he spoke, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ madhye mahābāhuḥ śrīmān keśavapūrvajaḥ nyaviśat paramaprītaḥ pūjyamāno mahārathaiḥ
english: In their midst the mighty-armed and illustrious elder brother of Keśava took his seat, supremely pleased, honoured by the great chariot-warriors.

sanskrit: sa babhau rājamadhyastho nīlavāsāḥ sitaprabhaḥ divīva nakṣatragaṇaiḥ parikīrṇo niśākaraḥ
english: Seated amid the kings, clad in dark blue and of fair complexion, he shone like the moon in the sky, ringed about by the hosts of stars.

sanskrit: tatas tayoḥ saṃnipātas tumulo romaharṣaṇaḥ āsīd antakaro rājan vairasya tava putrayoḥ
english: Then the clash of those two grew tumultuous and hair-raising, O king — a clash that would put an end to the enmity of your sons.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca pūrvam eva yadā rāmas tasmin yuddha upasthite āmantrya keśavaṃ yāto vṛṣṇibhiḥ sahitaḥ prabhuḥ
english: Janamejaya said: Earlier, when that war was at hand, the lord Rāma, having taken leave of Keśava, departed together with the Vṛṣṇis.

sanskrit: sāhāyyaṃ dhārtarāṣṭrasya na ca kartāsmi keśava na caiva pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ gamiṣyāmi yathāgatam
english: "I shall give no aid to the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O Keśava, nor to the sons of Pāṇḍu; I shall go my way as I came."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tadā rāmo yātaḥ śatrunibarhaṇaḥ tasya cāgamanaṃ bhūyo brahmañ śaṃsitum arhasi
english: Having said this, Rāma, the crusher of foes, departed then. Of his return now, O brāhmaṇa, you should tell me once more.

sanskrit: ākhyāhi me vistarataḥ kathaṃ rāma upasthitaḥ kathaṃ ca dṛṣṭavān yuddhaṃ kuśalo hy asi sattama
english: Recount to me in full how Rāma came to be present, and how he beheld the combat; for you are skilled, O most excellent one.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca upaplavye niviṣṭeṣu pāṇḍaveṣu mahātmasu preṣito dhṛtarāṣṭrasya samīpaṃ madhusūdanaḥ śamaṃ prati mahābāho hitārthaṃ sarvadehinām
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: While the great-souled Pāṇḍavas were encamped at Upaplavya, the slayer of Madhu was sent to the presence of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, in the cause of peace, O mighty-armed one, for the good of all living beings.

sanskrit: sa gatvā hāstinapuraṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ sametya ca uktavān vacanaṃ tathyaṃ hitaṃ caiva viśeṣataḥ na ca tat kṛtavān rājā yathākhyātaṃ hi te purā
english: Having gone to Hāstinapura and met with Dhṛtarāṣṭra, he spoke words that were true and especially salutary; but the king did not act upon them, just as has been told you before.

sanskrit: anavāpya śamaṃ tatra kṛṣṇaḥ puruṣasattamaḥ āgacchata mahābāhur upaplavyaṃ janādhipa
english: Failing to win peace there, Kṛṣṇa, that best of men, the mighty-armed one, came back to Upaplavya, O lord of men.

sanskrit: tataḥ pratyāgataḥ kṛṣṇo dhārtarāṣṭravisarjitaḥ akriyāyāṃ naravyāghra pāṇḍavān idam abravīt
english: Then Kṛṣṇa, having returned, dismissed by the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra with nothing accomplished, O tiger among men, said this to the Pāṇḍavas:

sanskrit: na kurvanti vaco mahyaṃ kuravaḥ kālacoditāḥ nirgacchadhvaṃ pāṇḍaveyāḥ puṣyeṇa sahitā mayā
english: "The Kurus, driven on by fate, will not heed my word. March forth, O Pāṇḍavas, together with me, under the constellation Puṣya."

sanskrit: tato vibhajyamāneṣu baleṣu balināṃ varaḥ provāca bhrātaraṃ kṛṣṇaṃ rauhiṇeyo mahāmanāḥ
english: Then, as the forces were being marshalled, the best of the mighty, the great-souled son of Rohiṇī, spoke to his brother Kṛṣṇa:

sanskrit: teṣām api mahābāho sāhāyyaṃ madhusūdana kriyatām iti tat kṛṣṇo nāsya cakre vacas tadā
english: "To those others too, O mighty-armed slayer of Madhu, let aid be given"; but Kṛṣṇa did not then act upon that word of his.

sanskrit: tato manyuparītātmā jagāma yadunandanaḥ tīrthayātrāṃ haladharaḥ sarasvatyāṃ mahāyaśāḥ maitre nakṣatrayoge sma sahitaḥ sarvayādavaiḥ
english: Then, his heart overcome with displeasure, the delight of the Yadus, the plough-bearer of great renown, set out on a pilgrimage to the sacred fords along the Sarasvatī, under the conjunction of the Maitra constellation, accompanied by all the Yādavas.

sanskrit: āśrayām āsa bhojas tu duryodhanam ariṃdamaḥ yuyudhānena sahito vāsudevas tu pāṇḍavān
english: The Bhoja, that tamer of foes, gave his allegiance to Duryodhana, while Vāsudeva, together with Yuyudhāna, supported the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: rauhiṇeye gate śūre puṣyeṇa madhusūdanaḥ pāṇḍaveyān puraskṛtya yayāv abhimukhaḥ kurūn
english: When the valiant son of Rohiṇī had departed, the slayer of Madhu, under the star Puṣya, placing the Pāṇḍavas at the fore, marched forth to face the Kurus.

sanskrit: gacchann eva pathisthas tu rāmaḥ preṣyān uvāca ha saṃbhārāṃs tīrthayātrāyāṃ sarvopakaraṇāni ca ānayadhvaṃ dvārakāyā agnīn vai yājakāṃs tathā
english: As he journeyed, while still upon the road, Rāma said to his attendants: "Bring from Dvārakā the provisions for the pilgrimage and all the requisites — the sacred fires and the officiating priests as well."

sanskrit: suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ caiva dhenūr vāsāṃsi vājinaḥ kuñjarāṃś ca rathāṃś caiva kharoṣṭraṃ vāhanāni ca kṣipram ānīyatāṃ sarvaṃ tīrthahetoḥ paricchadam
english: "Gold and silver, milch cows, garments, horses, elephants and chariots, mules and camels and beasts of burden — let all the equipage for the sake of the pilgrimage be brought quickly."

sanskrit: pratisrotaḥ sarasvatyā gacchadhvaṃ śīghragāminaḥ ṛtvijaś cānayadhvaṃ vai śataśaś ca dvijarṣabhān
english: "Travel swiftly, upstream along the Sarasvatī; and bring the officiating priests and bulls among the twice-born by the hundred."

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃdiśya tu preṣyān baladevo mahābalaḥ tīrthayātrāṃ yayau rājan kurūṇāṃ vaiśase tadā sarasvatīṃ pratisrotaḥ samudrād abhijagmivān
english: Having thus instructed his attendants, the mighty Baladeva set forth on the pilgrimage, O king, during the slaughter of the Kurus, journeying upstream along the Sarasvatī from the sea.

sanskrit: ṛtvigbhiś ca suhṛdbhiś ca tathānyair dvijasattamaiḥ rathair gajais tathāśvaiś ca preṣyaiś ca bharatarṣabha gokharoṣṭraprayuktaiś ca yānaiś ca bahubhir vṛtaḥ
english: Surrounded by officiating priests and friends and other most excellent of the twice-born, by chariots, elephants and horses and attendants, O bull of the Bharatas, and by many conveyances drawn by oxen, mules and camels.

sanskrit: śrāntānāṃ klāntavapuṣāṃ śiśūnāṃ vipulāyuṣām tāni yānāni deśeṣu pratīkṣyante sma bhārata bubhukṣitānām arthāya kḷptam annaṃ samantataḥ
english: For the weary and worn of body, for children and for the long-lived, those conveyances waited in their several places, O Bhārata; and food was made ready on every side for the sake of the hungry.

sanskrit: yo yo yatra dvijo bhoktuṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate tadā tasya tasya tu tatraivam upajahrus tadā nṛpa
english: Whatever twice-born one wished, wherever, to take his food, to that very one, just there, they brought it then, O king.

sanskrit: tatra sthitā narā rājan rauhiṇeyasya śāsanāt bhakṣyapeyasya kurvanti rāśīṃs tatra samantataḥ
english: The men stationed there, O king, by the command of the son of Rohiṇī, made heaps of food and drink everywhere about.

sanskrit: vāsāṃsi ca mahārhāṇi paryaṅkāstaraṇāni ca pūjārthaṃ tatra kḷptāni viprāṇāṃ sukham icchatām
english: And costly garments, couches and spreadings were arranged there for the honouring of the brāhmaṇas who sought comfort.

sanskrit: yatra yaḥ svapate vipraḥ kṣatriyo vāpi bhārata tatra tatra tu tasyaiva sarvaṃ kḷptam adṛśyata
english: Wherever a brāhmaṇa, or a kṣatriya too, lay down to sleep, O Bhārata, there for that very one was everything seen ready prepared.

sanskrit: yathāsukhaṃ janaḥ sarvas tiṣṭhate yāti vā tadā yātukāmasya yānāni pānāni tṛṣitasya ca
english: All the folk then rested or journeyed at their ease — conveyances for one who wished to travel, and drink for one who thirsted,

sanskrit: bubhukṣitasya cānnāni svādūni bharatarṣabha upajahrur narās tatra vastrāṇy ābharaṇāni ca
english: and savoury foods for one who hungered, O bull of the Bhāratas; there the men brought garments and ornaments besides.

sanskrit: sa panthāḥ prababhau rājan sarvasyaiva sukhāvahaḥ svargopamas tadā vīra narāṇāṃ tatra gacchatām
english: That road shone forth, O king, bringing comfort to every one; it was then like heaven, O hero, for the men who travelled there.

sanskrit: nityapramuditopetaḥ svādubhakṣaḥ śubhānvitaḥ vipaṇyāpaṇapaṇyānāṃ nānājanaśatair vṛtaḥ nānādrumalatopeto nānāratnavibhūṣitaḥ
english: Filled with unending joy, abounding in delicacies, attended by auspicious things, thronged with hundreds of diverse folk trading their wares in shops and markets, set about with many trees and creepers, and adorned with jewels of every kind.

sanskrit: tato mahātmā niyame sthitātmā; puṇyeṣu tīrtheṣu vasūni rājan dadau dvijebhyaḥ kratudakṣiṇāś ca; yadupravīro halabhṛt pratītaḥ
english: Then the great-souled one, his self set firm in vows, at the holy fords, O king, gave wealth to the twice-born and the sacrificial fees — that foremost hero of the Yadus, the renowned plough-bearer.

sanskrit: dogdhrīś ca dhenūś ca sahasraśo vai; suvāsasaḥ kāñcanabaddhaśṛṅgīḥ hayāṃś ca nānāvidhadeśajātān; yānāni dāsīś ca tathā dvijebhyaḥ
english: Milk-giving cows by the thousand, draped in fine cloth, their horns bound with gold, and horses born in lands of many kinds, conveyances and serving-women — these he gave to the twice-born.

sanskrit: ratnāni muktāmaṇividrumaṃ ca; śṛṅgīsuvarṇaṃ rajataṃ ca śubhram ayasmayaṃ tāmramayaṃ ca bhāṇḍaṃ; dadau dvijātipravareṣu rāmaḥ
english: Jewels — pearls, gems and coral — and horned gold and bright silver, and vessels of iron and of copper, Rāma bestowed upon the foremost of the twice-born.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa vittaṃ pradadau mahātmā; sarasvatītīrthavareṣu bhūri yayau krameṇāpratimaprabhāvas; tataḥ kurukṣetram udāravṛttaḥ
english: Thus did the great-souled one bestow abundant wealth at the excellent fords of the Sarasvatī; then he of incomparable might and noble conduct came by stages to Kurukṣetra.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca sārasvatānāṃ tīrthānāṃ guṇotpattiṃ vadasva me phalaṃ ca dvipadāṃ śreṣṭha karmanirvṛttim eva ca
english: Janamejaya said: Tell me of the origin of the virtues of the fords along the Sarasvatī, and their fruit, O best of two-footed beings, and the accomplishment of rites there.

sanskrit: yathākramaṃ ca bhagavaṃs tīrthānām anupūrvaśaḥ brahman brahmavidāṃ śreṣṭha paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me
english: And in due order, O blessed one, of the fords one after another, O brāhmaṇa, O best of the knowers of brahman; for great is my curiosity.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tīrthānāṃ vistaraṃ rājan guṇotpattiṃ ca sarvaśaḥ mayocyamānāṃ śṛṇu vai puṇyāṃ rājendra kṛtsnaśaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hear, O king, the full account of the fords and the origin of their virtues in every part, the holy tale told by me, O lord of kings, in its entirety.

sanskrit: pūrvaṃ mahārāja yadupravīra; ṛtviksuhṛdvipragaṇaiś ca sārdham puṇyaṃ prabhāsaṃ samupājagāma; yatroḍurāḍ yakṣmaṇā kliśyamānaḥ
english: First, O great king, that foremost hero of the Yadus, together with hosts of officiating priests, friends and brāhmaṇas, came to the holy Prabhāsa — where the lord of the stars was being afflicted by consumption.

sanskrit: vimuktaśāpaḥ punar āpya tejaḥ; sarvaṃ jagad bhāsayate narendra evaṃ tu tīrthapravaraṃ pṛthivyāṃ; prabhāsanāt tasya tataḥ prabhāsaḥ
english: There, freed from the curse and regaining his splendour, he lights up the whole world, O lord of men. Thus this foremost ford upon the earth, from his shining forth, is therefore called Prabhāsa.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca kimarthaṃ bhagavān somo yakṣmaṇā samagṛhyata kathaṃ ca tīrthapravare tasmiṃś candro nyamajjata
english: Janamejaya said: For what reason was the blessed Soma seized by consumption? And how did the moon plunge himself into that foremost of fords?

sanskrit: katham āplutya tasmiṃs tu punar āpyāyitaḥ śaśī etan me sarvam ācakṣva vistareṇa mahāmune
english: And how, having bathed therein, was the hare-marked moon replenished once more? Tell me all of this in full, O great sage.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca dakṣasya tanayā yās tāḥ prādurāsan viśāṃ pate sa saptaviṃśatiṃ kanyā dakṣaḥ somāya vai dadau
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Those who were the daughters of Dakṣa came into being, O lord of peoples; and Dakṣa gave twenty-seven maidens to Soma.

sanskrit: nakṣatrayoganiratāḥ saṃkhyānārthaṃ ca bhārata patnyo vai tasya rājendra somasya śubhalakṣaṇāḥ
english: Devoted to the conjunctions of the constellations and serving for the reckoning of time, O Bhārata, they were the wives of that Soma, O lord of kings, marked with auspicious signs.

sanskrit: tās tu sarvā viśālākṣyo rūpeṇāpratimā bhuvi atyaricyata tāsāṃ tu rohiṇī rūpasaṃpadā
english: All of them were wide-eyed and unequalled in beauty upon the earth; yet among them Rohiṇī surpassed the rest in the fullness of her beauty.

sanskrit: tatas tasyāṃ sa bhagavān prītiṃ cakre niśākaraḥ sāsya hṛdyā babhūvātha tasmāt tāṃ bubhuje sadā
english: Therefore the blessed maker of the night set his love upon her; she became dear to his heart, and so he ever resorted to her.

sanskrit: purā hi somo rājendra rohiṇyām avasac ciram tato 'sya kupitāny āsan nakṣatrāṇi mahātmanaḥ
english: For in olden time, O lord of kings, Soma dwelt long with Rohiṇī; and at this the constellations, wives of the great-souled one, grew wroth.

sanskrit: tā gatvā pitaraṃ prāhuḥ prajāpatim atandritāḥ somo vasati nāsmāsu rohiṇīṃ bhajate sadā
english: They went to their father, the Lord of Creatures, and without delay declared: "Soma dwells not with us; he resorts ever to Rohiṇī."

sanskrit: tā vayaṃ sahitāḥ sarvās tvatsakāśe prajeśvara vatsyāmo niyatāhārās tapaścaraṇatatparāḥ
english: "We all, gathered together, will dwell in your presence, O lord of creatures, with restricted food, intent upon the practice of austerities."

sanskrit: śrutvā tāsāṃ tu vacanaṃ dakṣaḥ somam athābravīt samaṃ vartasva bhāryāsu mā tvādharmo mahān spṛśet
english: Having heard their words, Dakṣa then said to Soma: "Behave equally toward your wives, lest a great unrighteousness touch you."

sanskrit: tāś ca sarvābravīd dakṣo gacchadhvaṃ somam antikāt samaṃ vatsyati sarvāsu candramā mama śāsanāt
english: And to all of them Dakṣa said: "Go to Soma's side; by my command the moon shall dwell equally with all of you."

sanskrit: visṛṣṭās tās tadā jagmuḥ śītāṃśubhavanaṃ tadā tathāpi somo bhagavān punar eva mahīpate rohiṇīṃ nivasaty eva prīyamāṇo muhur muhuḥ
english: Dismissed, they then went to the dwelling of the cool-rayed one; yet even so the blessed Soma, O lord of the earth, dwelt still with Rohiṇī, delighting in her again and again.

sanskrit: tatas tāḥ sahitāḥ sarvā bhūyaḥ pitaram abruvan tava śuśrūṣaṇe yuktā vatsyāmo hi tavāśrame somo vasati nāsmāsu nākarod vacanaṃ tava
english: Then all of them together spoke again to their father: "Engaged in serving you, we shall dwell in your hermitage; Soma dwells not with us, he has not done your bidding."

sanskrit: tāsāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā dakṣaḥ somam athābravīt samaṃ vartasva bhāryāsu mā tvāṃ śapsye virocana
english: Having heard those words of theirs, Dakṣa then said to Soma: "Behave equally toward your wives, lest I curse you, O shining one."

sanskrit: anādṛtya tu tad vākyaṃ dakṣasya bhagavāñ śaśī rohiṇyā sārdham avasat tatas tāḥ kupitāḥ punaḥ
english: But disregarding that word of Dakṣa, the blessed hare-marked one dwelt with Rohiṇī; then once more those wives grew wroth.

sanskrit: gatvā ca pitaraṃ prāhuḥ praṇamya śirasā tadā somo vasati nāsmāsu tasmān naḥ śaraṇaṃ bhava
english: And going to their father, bowing then with their heads, they said: "Soma dwells not with us; therefore be you our refuge."

sanskrit: rohiṇyām eva bhagavan sadā vasati candramāḥ tasmān nas trāhi sarvā vai yathā naḥ soma āviśet
english: "With Rohiṇī alone, O blessed one, the moon dwells ever; therefore protect us all, that Soma may come to us."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā bhagavān kruddho yakṣmāṇaṃ pṛthivīpate sasarja roṣāt somāya sa coḍupatim āviśat
english: Hearing this, the blessed one, wrathful, O lord of the earth, in his anger let loose consumption against Soma; and it entered the lord of the stars.

sanskrit: sa yakṣmaṇābhibhūtātmākṣīyatāhar ahaḥ śaśī yatnaṃ cāpy akarod rājan mokṣārthaṃ tasya yakṣmaṇaḥ
english: His being overcome by the consumption, the hare-marked one waned day by day; and he made effort, O king, to be freed of that consumption.

sanskrit: iṣṭveṣṭibhir mahārāja vividhābhir niśākaraḥ na cāmucyata śāpād vai kṣayaṃ caivābhyagacchata
english: Though the maker of the night performed sacrifices of many kinds, O great king, he was not released from the curse, and indeed came to wasting away.

sanskrit: kṣīyamāṇe tataḥ some oṣadhyo na prajajñire nirāsvādarasāḥ sarvā hatavīryāś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Then, as Soma wasted away, the herbs no longer grew; all of them were robbed of savour and wholly stripped of their potency.

sanskrit: oṣadhīnāṃ kṣaye jāte prāṇinām api saṃkṣayaḥ kṛśāś cāsan prajāḥ sarvāḥ kṣīyamāṇe niśākare
english: When the wasting of the herbs had come about, there was wasting of living beings too; and all creatures grew gaunt as the maker of the night waned away.

sanskrit: tato devāḥ samāgamya somam ūcur mahīpate kim idaṃ bhavato rūpam īdṛśaṃ na prakāśate
english: Then the gods, having assembled, said to Soma, O lord of the earth: "What is this? Your form does not shine forth as it once did."

sanskrit: kāraṇaṃ brūhi naḥ sarvaṃ yenedaṃ te mahad bhayam śrutvā tu vacanaṃ tvatto vidhāsyāmas tato vayam
english: "Tell us all the cause, whereby this great peril has come upon you; and having heard the word from you, we shall then provide a remedy."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ pratyuvāca sarvāṃs tāñ śaśalakṣaṇaḥ śāpaṃ ca kāraṇaṃ caiva yakṣmāṇaṃ ca tathātmanaḥ
english: Thus addressed, the hare-marked one answered all of them — the curse, and its cause, and the consumption that had come upon himself.

sanskrit: devās tasya vacaḥ śrutvā gatvā dakṣam athābruvan prasīda bhagavan some śāpaś caiṣa nivartyatām
english: The gods, hearing his words, went to Dakṣa and said: "Be gracious, O blessed one, toward Soma, and let this curse be turned back."

sanskrit: asau hi candramāḥ kṣīṇaḥ kiṃciccheṣo hi lakṣyate kṣayāc caivāsya deveśa prajāś cāpi gatāḥ kṣayam
english: "For yonder moon is wasted, and but a little of him is seen remaining; and through his wasting, O lord of the gods, the creatures too have come to ruin."

sanskrit: vīrudoṣadhayaś caiva bījāni vividhāni ca tathā vayaṃ lokaguro prasādaṃ kartum arhasi
english: "The plants and herbs and the seeds of many kinds, and we ourselves, O teacher of the world — you should show us grace."

sanskrit: evam uktas tadā cintya prāha vākyaṃ prajāpatiḥ naitac chakyaṃ mama vaco vyāvartayitum anyathā hetunā tu mahābhāgā nivartiṣyati kena cit
english: Thus addressed, the Lord of Creatures pondered and spoke this word: "This word of mine cannot be turned otherwise; yet, O illustrious ones, by some means it shall be reversed."

sanskrit: samaṃ vartatu sarvāsu śaśī bhāryāsu nityaśaḥ sarasvatyā vare tīrthe unmajjañ śaśalakṣaṇaḥ punar vardhiṣyate devās tad vai satyaṃ vaco mama
english: "Let the hare-marked one behave equally toward all his wives evermore; and emerging at the excellent ford of the Sarasvatī, the hare-marked one shall grow full again, O gods — that word of mine is true."

sanskrit: māsārdhaṃ ca kṣayaṃ somo nityam eva gamiṣyati māsārdhaṃ ca sadā vṛddhiṃ satyam etad vaco mama
english: "For half a month Soma shall ever pass to waning, and for half a month always to waxing — this word of mine is true."
